## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Resting-state EEG Dementia Classification (AD vs FTD vs CN)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: segment_length = 4 s, overlap = 0.5
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `AD` | 0 | Alzheimer's disease diagnosis |
  | `FTD` | 1 | Frontotemporal dementia diagnosis |
  | `CN` | 2 | Cognitively normal / Healthy controls |
- **Super Meta Notes**: Labels derived from subject-level diagnosis in `participants.tsv`. For each segmented epoch, assign the diagnostic label of the subject from which the epoch was recorded. No discrete raw event markers exist in this resting-state dataset; the `boundary` event (512) marks file segments, not clinical events.
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1016/j.clinph.2024.12.008 — SVM classifiers with time-frequency connectivity features achieved 95% accuracy for AD vs HC and 86% for FTD vs HC on ds004504 dataset.
  - DOI: 10.1109/access.2023.3294618 — DICE-Net binary classification (AD-CN, FTD-CN) using 30s windows with 15s overlap on 88 subjects (36 AD, 23 FTD, 29 CN).
  - DOI: 10.3390/data8060095 — Benchmarked 4s windows with 50% overlap for AD/FTD/CN classification using Leave-One-Subject-Out validation.
- **Kernel Notes**: Extract continuous EEG from all 176 files (concatenate both sessions per subject), segment into 4s sliding windows with 50% overlap. Extract subject ID from filename/filepath, look up diagnosis in participants.tsv (AD/FTD/CN), assign to all epochs from that subject. Consider class imbalance (36 AD, 23 FTD, 29 CN) in model training. Standard 19-channel 10-20 montage at 500 Hz.
